concept: Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans
summary: Source-anchored research for Conftest/OPA rules over terraform show -json plans. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Conftest recognizes deny, violation, and warn rules, including identifier suffixes such as deny_myrule. Its documentation shows Rego v1-style deny contains msg if syntax and conftest verify --policy ./policy for executing policy unit tests. (low confidence)
planned_values omits values that are still unknown. It describes the known planned outcome; resource_changes separately records the operations that lead to it. (low confidence)

Conftest searches the main namespace by default; --namespace selects a namespace and --all-namespaces evaluates across namespaces. Policies live in policy by default, with --policy overriding that directory. A custom OPA package must be selected explicitly when it is outside main. (high confidence)

Plan-time values can be incomplete. Planned values omit values not known until apply, and change.after_unknown replaces unknown leaf values with true; change.after is incomplete when it contains values unknown until apply. Policies that need such attributes cannot see their final values in the plan. Sources: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format

OPA policies operate on the JSON plan generated by Terraform, so they can only evaluate what appears in that plan; computed attributes that are not determined until apply time are not available to the policy. (Applying this to Atlas query-log collection or Performance Advisor is the pack's own inference, not stated by a source.) Sources: https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/terraform

Replacement operations have action arrays ["delete", "create"] or ["create", "delete"]. A deletion guard should test membership of "delete" in change.actions rather than equality with ["delete"], which would miss replacements. (high confidence)

Terraform documents backward-compatible minor changes and incompatible major changes in format_version. Consumers should ignore unknown properties for supported minor versions and reject unsupported major versions rather than silently evaluating a different input contract. (low confidence)

Generate a saved plan with terraform plan -out=tfplan, render it with terraform show -json tfplan > tfplan.json, and run conftest test tfplan.json --policy policy/ to evaluate Rego policies before apply. OPA documents the saved-plan conversion, while a practitioner demonstrates the Conftest invocation. (high confidence) Sources: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/plan ; https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/terraform ; https://dev.to/lucassha/don-t-let-your-terraform-go-rogue-with-conftest-and-the-open-policy-agent-233b
Conftest uses the OPA Rego language to evaluate assertions against structured configuration data, including Terraform inputs. (high confidence)

Plan JSON exposes resource_changes entries with resource type and change.actions; change.before and change.after describe old and proposed values. This supports policies scoped to resource types and operations. (high confidence)

Conftest discovers deny, violation and warn rules and defaults to the main namespace. Use --namespace for another package or --all-namespaces to evaluate every namespace. A policy in an unselected namespace needs explicit selection. (low confidence)

With -json, terraform show displays any sensitive values in Terraform state in plain text. In plan JSON, before_sensitive and after_sensitive mark sensitive leaves and should be combined with before and after to prevent accidental display of sensitive values in user interfaces. Saved plan files hold sensitive data in cleartext and should be treated as potentially-sensitive artifacts. Sources: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/show ; https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format ; https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/plan

Atlantis documents server-side Conftest checks on plan output. Its documented apply blocking requires policy checking together with the mergeable apply requirement, and policy owners can approve failures. Thus enforcement depends on workflow and approval configuration. (low confidence)

Conftest can unit-test policies with conftest verify --policy ./policy. Rego tests can substitute input and data with the with keyword. The documentation demonstrates passing and failing configuration tests. (low confidence)

A saved-plan JSON export includes the plan, configuration, and prior state. Omitting the file argument from terraform show -json instead exports the latest state snapshot, so a plan gate must explicitly pass the saved plan. (high confidence)

Plan policies can iterate input.resource_changes, select resources by type or address, and inspect change.actions and change.after to evaluate prospective operations and attributes. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.openpolicyagent.org/docs/terraform ; https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format

Terraform plan -json emits machine-readable UI messages, including planned_change events that omit the detailed attribute changes. It is a different interface from terraform show -json <saved-plan>; do not substitute the UI event stream for the saved-plan document expected by resource_changes policies. (high confidence)

terraform show -json can expose sensitive state values in plaintext. The plan JSON includes a prior_state representation and, for resource changes, before_sensitive/after_sensitive metadata marking which leaf values are sensitive; this metadata is meant to be combined with before/after to prevent accidental display of sensitive values. Sources: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/show ; https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/internals/json-format
